facts.name: Catalog heading and campus
facts.detail: The selected catalog is University Catalog 2026-2027. The program heading is Computer Science, M.S., and the page lists Location(s): Main Campus.
facts.quote: University Catalog 2026-2027 Computer Science, M.S. Location(s): Main Campus

facts.name: Program purpose
facts.detail: The catalog says the M.S. is structured to prepare students for advancement in employment as a computer scientist and for later doctoral study.
facts.quote: The program is structured to prepare students for advancement in employment as a computer scientist as well as for further study at the doctoral level.

facts.name: 3.0 GPA for conditional admission
facts.detail: Applicants with a bachelor's in Computer Science or a closely related field and an overall GPA of 3.0 or better are considered for conditional admission. An earlier department-page fact quoted similar wording but said 'full admission' instead of 'conditional admission.' Both quotes are kept and no winner is chosen.
facts.quote: Applicants must possess a Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science or a closely related field with overall GPA of 3.0 or better to be considered for conditional admission.

facts.name: Special action admission at 2.5-2.99 GPA
facts.detail: A promising applicant with a GPA between 2.5 and 2.99 may be admitted as a special action student and must then earn a 3.0 GPA in four qualifying courses approved in advance by the department.
facts.quote: A promising applicant with a GPA between 2.5 and 2.99 may be admitted as a special action student. Special action students must achieve an overall GPA of 3.0 for four qualifying courses as approved in advance by the department.

facts.name: Prerequisites for non-CS or non-ABET backgrounds
facts.detail: Prerequisite courses may be required for non-CS students or for students from non-ABET-accredited CS programs.
facts.quote: Prerequisite courses may be required for non-CS students or for students from non-ABET-accredited CS programs.

facts.name: Classified students and 4000-level prerequisites
facts.detail: Classified Master of Science students are not required to take prerequisites below the 4000-level when they use 4000-level courses to satisfy the degree requirement.
facts.quote: Classified Master of Science students are not required to take any prerequisites below the 4000-level when they take 4000-level courses to satisfy the degree requirement.

facts.name: 30 units with 18-unit 5000-level core
facts.detail: The degree requires 30 units, including 18 units in 5000-level core courses. This 2026-2027 catalog page is a later official curriculum source than the department curriculum page earlier tagged as 2023-2024; both sources are kept and no winner is chosen.
facts.quote: The Master of Science degree in Computer Science degree requires completion of 30 units, with 18 units in 5000-level core courses.

facts.name: Pre-classified coursework cap
facts.detail: Up to 6 units of acceptable post-baccalaureate coursework completed before classified standing may be included in the master's program.
facts.quote: Up to 6 units of acceptable post-baccalaureate coursework completed before entrance into classified standing may be included in the master's degree program.

facts.name: Thesis or comprehensive examination required
facts.detail: A thesis or a comprehensive examination satisfies the Culminating Experiences requirement.
facts.quote: A thesis or comprehensive examination is required to satisfy the Culminating Experiences requirement.

facts.name: Core course structure
facts.detail: The 18 core units are met by selecting two courses from each of three areas of study (6 units each).
facts.quote: Requirement for Core Courses (18 units) Select two courses from each of the three areas of study:

facts.name: Software Design and Implementation core area
facts.detail: Area I is Software Design and Implementation (6 units); students select two courses from that list.
facts.quote: I. Software Design and Implementation (6 units) Select two courses.

facts.name: System Infrastructure core area
facts.detail: Area II is System Infrastructure (6 units); students select two courses from that list.
facts.quote: II. System Infrastructure (6 units) Select two courses.

facts.name: Computing in the World core area
facts.detail: Area III is Computing in the World (6 units); students select two courses from that list.
facts.quote: III. Computing in the World (6 units) Select two courses.

facts.name: Directed electives 6 or 12 units
facts.detail: Directed electives are 6 or 12 units: CS 5960 (comprehensive exam) students must select 12 units; CS 5990 (thesis) students select 6 units.
facts.quote: Requirements for Directed Electives (6 or 12 units) CS 5960 students must select 12 units to satisfy the degree requirement. CS 5990 students select 6 units.

facts.name: Culminating experience courses
facts.detail: Students select one culminating path: CS 5960 Comprehensive Examination (0 units) or CS 5990 Thesis at 3 units, completed for 6 units. Students who take CS 5960 must complete 12 units of electives.
facts.quote: Culminating Experiences (0 or 6 units) Select one course. CS 5960 - Comprehensive Examination [0] * CS 5990 - Thesis [3] (complete 6 units) * Students who take CS 5960 must complete a total of 12 units of electives.
